message.content:
Build a first-party live chat (Tidio equivalent) for Nxeon at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma, TypeScript): a chat widget on the site → conversations land in an admin inbox where staff reply.

SCHEMA (already added, client generated — do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma): `ChatConversation` (id, userId?, visitorId, name?, email?, status OPEN|CLOSED, assignedToId?, unreadForAgent, unreadForUser, lastMessageAt, createdAt, messages[]) and `ChatMessage` (id, conversationId, sender "visitor"|"agent", body, createdAt).

FIRST read: lib/auth.ts (currentUser/requireUser/realUser), lib/rbac.ts (requireArea for admin, area "support"), lib/rate-limit.ts (checkRateLimit), components/ui/primitives.tsx, an existing admin page e.g. app/admin/support/page.tsx and app/admin/feedback/page.tsx for admin UI patterns, and app/api/track/route.ts for the API-route + clientIp pattern.

BUILD:
1. **API routes** (app/api/chat/route.ts + app/api/chat/[id]/route.ts): 
   - POST /api/chat → start or continue a conversation for a `visitorId` (from the client). Body: {visitorId, name?, email?, body}. Rate-limit per IP (checkRateLimit, e.g. 30/min). Creates the conversation if new, appends a visitor ChatMessage, sets unreadForAgent=true, lastMessageAt=now. If a user is signed in (currentUser), set userId. Returns the conversation + messages.
   - GET /api/chat?visitorId=... → poll: returns the visitor's open conversation + messages (for the widget to poll every few seconds). Mark unreadForUser=false on read.
   Validate/clip inputs; never leak other visitors' data (scope strictly by visitorId).
2. **Widget** components/ChatWidget.tsx ("use client"): a floating chat bubble (bottom-right) that opens a panel; generates/stores a `visitorId` in localStorage; posts messages to /api/chat and polls GET every ~4s; shows message history; optional name/email capture on first message. Style with the existing design tokens (.card, .btn-primary, navy/violet, .glass). Do NOT mount it in any layout yourself — the orchestrator mounts it (just export the component).
3. **Admin inbox** app/admin/chat/page.tsx: `await requireArea("support")`; lists conversations (newest/unread first) with a detail view + reply box. Create lib/actions-chat.ts ("use server", async only): `replyToConversation(id, body)` (staff → appends an "agent" ChatMessage, unreadForUser=true, unreadForAgent=false, assignedToId=realUser), `closeConversation(id)`, `assignConversation(id)`. Reply UI is a small client component you create (components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx) that can poll for new messages.

RULES: "use server" files export only async functions. Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma, app/layout.tsx, app/admin/layout.tsx, worker/*, lib/rbac.ts. Do NOT run build/tsc/prisma/commit. Rate-limit public endpoints; scope visitor data strictly. Report files created, the admin route, and tell the orchestrator exactly where to mount <ChatWidget/> (recommend app/layout.tsx near CookieConsent) and add the /admin/chat nav entry + HREF_AREA mapping.

2	import type { Role, User } from "@prisma/client";
3	import { realUser } from "./auth";

5	/**
6	 * Role-based access control for the admin ops portal.
7	 *
8	 * The admin surface is divided into logical *areas*. Each area maps to the set
9	 * of staff roles allowed to see and use it. ADMIN implicitly has every area.
10	 * The admin layout uses this to (a) let any staff role in and (b) hide nav
11	 * items a role can't reach; each sensitive page additionally gates itself with
12	 * `requireArea(...)` so a hand-typed URL is refused too.
13	 */
14	export type Area =
15	  | "overview"
16	  | "analytics"
17	  | "clients"
18	  | "support"
19	  | "fleet"
20	  | "billing"
21	  | "platform";
22	
23	/** Which roles may access each area. ADMIN is always allowed (see canAccess). */
24	export const AREA_ROLES: Record<Area, Role[]> = {
25	  overview: ["SUPPORT", "BILLING", "ADMIN"],
26	  analytics: ["ADMIN"],
27	  clients: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
28	  support: ["SUPPORT", "ADMIN"],
29	  fleet: ["ADMIN"],
30	  billing: ["BILLING", "ADMIN"],
31	  platform: ["ADMIN"],
32	};
33	
34	export function canAccess(role: Role, area: Area): boolean {
35	  return role === "ADMIN" || AREA_ROLES[area].includes(role);
36	}
37	
38	/** Any non-customer role that belongs in the ops portal. */
39	export function isStaff(role: Role): boolean {
40	  return role === "SUPPORT" || role === "BILLING" || role === "ADMIN";
41	}
42	
43	/** Maps admin nav hrefs to their governing area. Unknown routes default to platform (ADMIN-only). */
44	const HREF_AREA: Record<string, Area> = {
45	  "/admin": "overview",
46	  "/admin/analytics": "analytics",
47	  "/admin/users": "clients",

83	export function areaForHref(href: string): Area {
84	  return HREF_AREA[href] ?? "platform";
85	}
86	
87	export function canAccessHref(role: Role, href: string): boolean {
88	  return canAccess(role, areaForHref(href));
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * Server-side page guard. Redirects to /login if signed out, or back to the
93	 * overview if the (staff) user's role can't reach this area. Returns the real
94	 * signed-in user (impersonation is refused elsewhere in the admin layout).
95	 */
96	export async function requireArea(area: Area): Promise<User> {
97	  const user = await realUser();
98	  if (!user) redirect("/login");
99	  if (!isStaff(user.role)) redirect("/dashboard");
100	  if (!canAccess(user.role, area)) redirect("/admin");
101	  return user;
102	}
